_convention._note: KEY NAMING RULES — read before adding keys:
_convention._1: Use camelCase for keys: commentSubmit not comment_submit
_convention._2: Group by page/feature namespace: nav, home, blog, about
_convention._3: Shared UI primitives go in 'common', NOT in feature namespaces
_convention._4: en.json is source of truth — zh.json must mirror structure exactly
_convention._5: Run 'npm run i18n:check' before committing to catch zombie keys

home.title: Full-Stack Engineer · Backend & Data
home.intro: I work on the backend and data side: pipelines, integrations and the internal tools people run their day on. At Value Windows & Doors I helped design a Databricks + dbt data platform and built part of it, along with the pipelines and portals around it.
home.introLong1: I work on the backend and data side: pipelines, integrations and the internal tools people run their day on.
home.introLong2: Since January 2024 I've been at Value Windows & Doors. There I helped design a data platform on Databricks + dbt, layered Bronze→Silver→Gold→Mart, and built part of it. It turns raw ERP data into models that the manufacturing, inventory, sales and workforce reports read directly. I also write data-migration and integration pipelines in C# and Python, and build Power BI dashboards and React internal portals.
home.introLong3: Before that I interned at APEXUS-TECH, writing Python + MySQL services that ingested financial-market data, and ETL pipelines. During my M.S. in Analytics at Northeastern University I was a tutor for the data warehousing and SQL course (ALY6030).
home.introLong4: This site is my public workspace: engineering notes, integration patterns, and small experiments in the Playground.
home.metaDescription: Jack Deng — full-stack engineer focused on backend and data. Data platforms, integrations and internal tools with Python, C#, SQL, Databricks and TypeScript.

about.title: Jack Deng
about.subtitle: Full-Stack Engineer · Backend & Data
about.bio1: Hi, I'm Jack — a Software Engineer based in California, focused on designing reliable enterprise data systems and full-stack applications. I bridge business operations and technical infrastructure through robust backend architectures and scalable data pipelines.
about.bio2: This site is my public workspace: engineering notes, integration patterns, and tools I build along the way. It runs on <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> + <payload>Payload CMS</payload> with a <supabase>Supabase</supabase> PostgreSQL backend.
about.bio3: Outside of work I'm probably debugging a flow, reading systems-design docs, or figuring out why the ETL ran 3 seconds slower than yesterday.

terminal.helpBuild: seeds, models and tests, in dependency order
terminal.unknownDbt: dbt: try dbt build, dbt run, dbt test or dbt seed
terminal.hint: Nothing runs here. The log is what dbt would print for jaffle_shop, the demo project dbt Labs publishes. Type help for the commands. With a test broken, dbt build still runs that model's other tests, then skips every model and test downstream of it.

vortex.canvasLabel: Rings of the text "{phrase}" turning around the centre.
vortex.hint: Move the pointer through the rings to scatter the letters. Press and hold to pull every ring toward the centre, or use the Pull in button from the keyboard. With reduced motion the rings don't turn on their own, but the pointer still works.

blueprint.hint: Drag a letter, or Tab to one and move it with the arrow keys, one grid step at a time or one pixel with Shift. This site's layout uses the same 8px grid.

skills.hint: The same skills as the About page, coloured by group. Pick one up and throw it. The physics engine is matter-js, and it only loads once the box is on screen. With reduced motion nothing falls until you press Drop.

devDay.intro: It's 9:00 and you've just sat down. There's already work in the inbox, and two meetings this afternoon.
devDay.rule1: Every choice takes an hour. Careful work is steady; the quick way is twice as fast but adds tech debt, and the more debt there is, the likelier an incident later.
devDay.rule2: Missed deadlines and skipped meetings cost the boss's goodwill. Run out of that, or of energy, and the day ends early.
devDay.rule3: The first two coffees help; the third gives you the jitters. A break restores you, if the boss doesn't catch you taking it.

devDay.inboxEmpty: Inbox zero. Pay down some debt, or take a break.

legend.text: Everything shipped, no deadline slipped, and the code is still clean. Days like this are rare.

firefighter.title: Hero of the day
firefighter.text: It all shipped, all of it the quick way. The debt is piling up. Good luck on call tonight.

rough.title: Underwater
rough.text: Several deadlines slipped and the inbox isn't empty. Tomorrow's standup could be awkward.

invisible.text: You paid down a lot of debt but shipped too little for the boss's liking.

normal.text: Some things got done; the rest can wait until tomorrow. Most days are like this.
